title: Angles: lines, parallels and triangles
hook: A straight line is 180°, a triangle is 180°, and parallel lines copy angles.

steps.prompt: An exterior angle of a triangle is 130°. The two interior angles not next to it add to:
steps.why: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles.

steps.prompt: From memory: what do the angles in a triangle add up to?
Two angles of a triangle are 47° and 68°. Find the third.
Two angles form a straight line. One is 115°. The other is:
Match each pair or set of angles to its rule.
steps.why: Vertical angles are equal. A straight line is 180°, a full turn is 360°, and complementary means 90°.

steps.prompt: Parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle is 72°. Its alternate interior angle is:
Same lines: the same-side interior angle to that 72° angle is:
An isosceles triangle has a 40° top angle. Finding a base angle. Tap the line with the mistake.

keys: Straight line: 180°. Triangle: 180°. Around a point: 360°.
Parallel lines: corresponding and alternate angles are equal; same-side interior angles add to 180°.
Isosceles: the base angles are equal.

recall.prompt: A triangle has angles of 90° and 35°. What is the third angle?

recall.why: Opposite angles at a crossing are equal.
